links.outcome: Time to CT and lung cancer diagnosis with vs without AI worklist prioritization
links.effect: Median time to CT 53 vs 53 days (ratio of geometric means 0.97, 95% CI 0.93-1.02; P=0.31); time to diagnosis 44 vs 46 days (ratio 0.98, 95% CI 0.83-1.16; P=0.84); no stage difference (P=0.34).
links.quote: AI prioritization of CXR requested by UK primary care has no significant impact on the lung cancer pathway.

links.outcome: Time to CT and lung cancer diagnosis
links.effect: Prioritization on versus off: median CT time 53 versus 53 days (P = 0.31); median diagnosis time 44 versus 46 days (P = 0.84).
links.quote: Median (interquartile range) times to CT were 53 days (17-145) and 53 days (19-141), with and without AI prioritization, corresponding to a ratio of geometric means of 0.97 (95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.93-1.02; P = 0.31).

links.effect: Median times to CT were 53 days with and without AI prioritization.
links.quote: Median (interquartile range) times to CT were 53 days (17-145) and 53 days (19-141), with and without AI prioritization, corresponding to a ratio of geometric means of 0.97 (95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.93-1.02; P = 0.31).

links.effect: Median times to diagnosis were 44 days with and 46 days without AI prioritization (P = 0.84), showing no clinical benefit.
links.quote: Median times to diagnosis were 44 days (26-90) and 46 days (24-105) respectively, with a ratio of geometric means of 0.98 (95% CI = 0.83-1.16; P = 0.84).
